name: Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic
native: საქართველოს საბჭოთა სოციალისტური რესპუბლიკა (Sakartvelos Sabch'ota Sotsialist'uri Respublik'a)

predecessors.name: Georgia
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's Georgia of 1920-1921, the Democratic Republic of Georgia

ledger.x: 1921, 25 February: "On 25 February, after a one-week offence by the Red Army, Tbilisi fell to the Bolsheviks" and the Revolutionary Committee "declared the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic on 25 February 1921".

1921, March: the rest of Georgia passes to the Soviet side as the invasion (12 February to 17 March 1921) ends; "In March 1921 the government of the Georgian Democratic Republic was forced into exile" and Batumi is surrendered to the Revkom.

Page silent on whether the Georgian SSR held or administered the Artvin Okrug before the Treaty of Kars; it is drawn from the invasion's end (March 1921) because the page says the republic was "forced to cede the Georgian-dominated Artvin Okrug to Turkey".

1921, 13 October: the Treaty of Kars: the southern half of the former Batum oblast, "largely the Artvin okrug", "would be annexed to Turkey"; "The Georgian SSR was forced to cede the Georgian-dominated Artvin Okrug to Turkey in exchange for keeping Adjara."
1922, 12 March: "From March 12, 1922, to December 5, 1936, it was part of the Transcaucasian SFSR together with the Armenian SSR and the Azerbaijan SSR."
1936, 5 December: "In 1936, the TSFSR was dissolved and Georgia became the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic".

1990, 14 November: "Renamed to Republic of Georgia: 14 November 1990" (sovereignty declared 9 March 1990; "On November 14 a transitional period was declared until the restoration of Georgia's independence").

wars.name: Red Army invasion of Georgia
wars.outcome: The invasion ran from 12 February to 17 March 1921; the Red Army entered Tbilisi on 25 February; the Georgian government went into exile; the Treaty of Kars (13 October 1921) "contained the provisions agreed upon in March".

certainty.note: The Batum oblast changed hands between February and October 1921; the page gives no district-level dates.
Treaty of Kars border with Turkey; the Abkhazia and South Ossetia lines are the republic's internal boundaries, not on the pages opened.
